Predicates:
Pets(x) ::: x is a pet.
AllowedIn(x, y) ::: x is allowed in building y.
DepositRequired(y) ::: a deposit is required to rent in building y.
DepositAmount(y, d) ::: the security deposit in building y is d.

Tom(x) ::: x is Tom.
ManagedBuilding(y) ::: y is a managed building.
Build(y) ::: y is a building.
HasPet(x, y) ::: x has pet y.
Year(y, 2000) ::: year y was in.
Price(y, p) ::: price y costs.
Allowed(x, y) ::: x is allowed in y.
Rentable(x, y) ::: x can rent y.
Rent(y, p) ::: rent of y is p.
SecurityDeposit(y, d) ::: security deposit for y is d.

Premises:
Pets(Fluffy) ::: Fluffy is a pet.
Cats(x) ::: x are cats.
Pets(x) → Cats(x) ::: Cats are pets.
Build(oliveGarden) ::: The Olive Garden is a managed building.
ManagedBuilding(oliveGarden) ::: The Olive Garden is a managed building.
Rent(oliveGarden, 2000) ::: The rent at The Olive Garden is $2000.
Year(methodOfStudyingGregorianChant, 1946) ::: The book was published in 1946.
Author(miroslav, methodOfStudyingGregorianChant) ::: Miroslav authored the book.
Publish(methodOfStudyingGregorianChant, 1946) ::: The book was published in 1946.
∀x (ChoralConductor(x) → Musician(x)) ::: Any choral conductor is a musician.
∃x (Musician(x) ∧ Love(x, music)) ::: Some musicians love music.
Love(miroslav, music) ::: Miroslav loved music.
∃y (Czech(y) ∧ Author(y, methodOfStudyingGregorianChant) ∧ Book(methodOfStudyingGregorianChant) ∧ Publish(methodOfStudyingGregorianChant, 1946)) ::: A Czech wrote a book in 1946.
¬∃x (ChoralConductor(x) ∧ Specialize(x, renaissance)) ::: No choral conductor specialized in Renaissance.

Conclusion:
Love(miroslav, music) ::: Miroslav loved music.
∃y (Czech(y) ∧ Author(y, y) ∧ Book(y) ∧ Publish(y, 1946)) ::: A Czech wrote a book in 1946.
¬∃x (ChoralConductor(x) ∧ Specialize(x, renaissance)) ::: No choral conductor specialized in Renaissance.

(For the last problem about Tom and The Olive Garden, the relevant premises are: Pets(Fluffy), Pets(x) → Cats(x), Build(oliveGarden), ManagedBuilding(oliveGarden), Rent(oliveGarden, 2000), and the statement about the rent being more than $1500. The main conclusion is whether Tom will rent an apartment in The Olive Garden.)
